entries.title: Whistle
entries.meaning: Any sound-signalling appliance capable of producing the prescribed blasts and complying with Annex III.
entries.note: Shown with a short blast for reference.

entries.title: Short blast
entries.meaning: A blast of about one second's duration.

entries.title: Prolonged blast
entries.meaning: A blast of from four to six seconds' duration (5 s here).

entries.title: One short blast
entries.meaning: I am altering my course to starboard.
entries.who: A power-driven vessel underway, in sight of another, manoeuvring as authorised or required by the Rules.

entries.title: Two short blasts
entries.meaning: I am altering my course to port.
entries.who: As above.

entries.title: Three short blasts
entries.meaning: I am operating astern propulsion.
entries.who: As above (this does not mean the vessel is necessarily making sternway).

entries.title: Light flashes (optional)
entries.meaning: Any whistle signal may be supplemented by light flashes: one flash, two flashes, three flashes with the same meanings as 1, 2 and 3 short blasts; each flash about one second, interval about one second, interval between successive signals not less than ten seconds.

entries.title: Two prolonged, one short
entries.meaning: I intend to overtake you on your starboard side.
entries.who: In a narrow channel or fairway (Rule 9(e)(i)): the vessel intending to overtake.

entries.title: Two prolonged, two short
entries.meaning: I intend to overtake you on your port side.
entries.who: As above.

entries.title: Prolonged, short, prolonged, short
entries.meaning: Agreement: the vessel about to be overtaken, acting under Rule 9(e)(i), signals her agreement in this order.
entries.who: The vessel to be overtaken, in a narrow channel or fairway.

entries.title: Five or more short and rapid blasts
entries.meaning: Danger / doubt signal: I do not understand your intentions or actions, or I doubt that sufficient action is being taken to avoid collision.
entries.who: A vessel in sight of another that is in doubt; may be accompanied by at least five short and rapid light flashes.

entries.title: One prolonged blast (bend or obstruction)
entries.meaning: I am nearing a bend, or an area where other vessels may be hidden by an obstruction.
entries.who: Answered with one prolonged blast by any approaching vessel within hearing around the bend or behind the obstruction.

entries.title: Whistles more than 100 m apart
entries.meaning: If whistles are fitted on a vessel at a distance apart of more than 100 metres, one whistle only shall be used for manoeuvring and warning signals.

entries.title: Power-driven vessel making way
entries.meaning: One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.
entries.who: Power-driven vessel making way through the water.

entries.title: Power-driven vessel underway, stopped, no way
entries.meaning: Two prolonged blasts in succession, about 2 seconds between them, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.
entries.who: Power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water.

entries.title: NUC, RAM, CBD, sailing, fishing, towing or pushing
entries.meaning: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.
entries.who: Vessel not under command; restricted in her ability to manoeuvre; constrained by her draught; sailing vessel; vessel engaged in fishing; vessel engaged in towing or pushing another vessel.

entries.title: Fishing or RAM vessel at anchor
entries.meaning: Instead of the anchor signals: one prolonged and two short blasts, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.
entries.who: A vessel engaged in fishing, or restricted in her ability to manoeuvre when carrying out her work, while at anchor.

entries.title: Towed vessel (last of the tow, if manned)
entries.meaning: One prolonged followed by three short blasts, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes, if possible immediately after the towing vessel's signal.
entries.who: A vessel towed, or only the last vessel of a tow, if manned.

entries.title: Composite unit (pusher and pushed)
entries.meaning: A pushing vessel and a vessel pushed ahead, rigidly connected, are regarded as one power-driven vessel and give the signal of 35(a) or 35(b).
entries.who: Rigidly connected composite unit.

entries.title: At anchor (under 100 m): bell
entries.meaning: Bell rung rapidly for about 5 seconds at intervals of not more than one minute.
entries.who: A vessel at anchor, less than 100 m long.

entries.title: At anchor (100 m or more): bell, then gong
entries.meaning: Bell rung rapidly for about 5 seconds in the forepart, then immediately the gong rung rapidly for about 5 seconds in the after part, at intervals of not more than one minute.
entries.who: A vessel at anchor, 100 m or more in length.

entries.title: At anchor: optional warning of position
entries.meaning: A vessel at anchor may in addition sound one short, one prolonged and one short blast to warn an approaching vessel of her position and of the possibility of collision.
entries.who: A vessel at anchor.

entries.title: Aground: bell with three strokes before and after
entries.meaning: Three separate and distinct strokes on the bell, rapid bell ringing for about 5 seconds, then three separate strokes again, at intervals of not more than one minute (plus the gong signal of 35(g) if 100 m or more).
entries.who: A vessel aground (she may in addition sound an appropriate whistle signal).

entries.title: Aground, 100 m or more: bell and gong
entries.meaning: As 35(h) with the gong signal of 35(g) added.
entries.who: A vessel aground, 100 m or more in length.

entries.title: Small vessels
entries.meaning: A vessel of 12 m or more but less than 20 m need not give the bell signals of (g) and (h) but, if she does not, shall make some other efficient sound signal at intervals of not more than 2 minutes. A vessel under 12 m need not give the signals above but, if she does not, shall make some other efficient sound signal at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

entries.title: Pilot vessel on duty: identity signal
entries.meaning: A pilot vessel engaged on pilotage duty may, in addition to the signals of 35(a), (b) or (g), identify herself by four short blasts.
entries.who: A pilot vessel engaged on pilotage duty.

entries.title: Attention signal (training example)
entries.meaning: Any sound or light signal that cannot be mistaken for any signal authorised elsewhere in the Rules may be used to attract attention. (This example is a two-tone sweep; it is NOT a prescribed signal.)
entries.note: The danger signal (five or more short and rapid blasts) must not be used merely to attract attention.

entries.title: Searchlight toward the danger
entries.meaning: A vessel may direct the beam of her searchlight in the direction of the danger, in such a way as not to embarrass any vessel. A light used to attract attention must not be mistaken for an aid to navigation, and high-intensity intermittent or revolving lights (such as strobes) shall be avoided.

entries.title: Gun or other explosive signal
entries.meaning: A gun or other explosive signal fired at intervals of about a minute. (Demonstration fires three reports about 2 seconds apart; the real interval is about one minute.)

entries.title: Continuous sounding of a fog-signalling apparatus
entries.meaning: A continuous sounding with any fog-signalling apparatus. (The demonstration stops after 20 seconds; press Stop to end it sooner. A real distress signal continues until help arrives.)

entries.title: Rockets or shells throwing red stars
entries.meaning: Rockets or shells, throwing red stars, fired one at a time at short intervals.

entries.title: SOS in Morse code
entries.meaning: The group ... --- ... (SOS) in the Morse code, by radiotelegraphy or any other signalling method (here on the horn, dot 0.25 s, dash 0.75 s).

entries.title: MAYDAY by radiotelephony
entries.meaning: A signal sent by radiotelephony consisting of the spoken word MAYDAY.

entries.title: International Code distress signal N.C.
entries.meaning: The International Code Signal of distress indicated by N.C. (flags November over Charlie: 'I am in distress and require immediate assistance').

entries.title: Square flag with a ball
entries.meaning: A signal consisting of a square flag having above or below it a ball or anything resembling a ball.

entries.title: Flames on the vessel
entries.meaning: Flames on the vessel (as from a burning tar barrel, oil barrel, etc.).

entries.title: Rocket parachute flare or hand flare
entries.meaning: A rocket parachute flare or a hand flare showing a red light.

entries.title: Orange smoke
entries.meaning: A smoke signal giving off orange-coloured smoke.

entries.title: Raising and lowering arms
entries.meaning: Slowly and repeatedly raising and lowering arms outstretched to each side.

entries.title: Radio distress alerts
entries.meaning: A distress alert by digital selective calling (DSC); a ship-to-shore alert by satellite service; signals from emergency position-indicating radio beacons (EPIRBs); approved signals by radiocommunication, including survival craft radar transponders.

entries.title: Prohibition of misuse
entries.meaning: The use or exhibition of any of these signals except to indicate distress and need of assistance, and the use of other signals that may be confused with them, is prohibited.

rule_checks.note: What the 'Check rules' panel judges, in terms of the rules above. Levels: OK, INFO (monitor), WARN (rules at risk), BAD (rules broken).

headlines.BAD: NOT FOLLOWING THE RULES OF THE ROAD
headlines.OK: FOLLOWING THE RULES OF THE ROAD
headlines.NONE: NO RISK: NO RULE ACTION NEEDED

checks.what: Risk of collision exists when the target is closing and the CPA is inside the CPA limit (settings.cpaLimit); doubt means risk.
Give-way vessel is expected to act early (before TCPA reaches the alarm). Message: act early and substantially.
Action taken after the TCPA alarm is flagged as late (warning).
A course or speed change too small to be apparent is flagged (apparent alteration setting).
After acting, CPA is still reported until the target is past and clear; a still-small CPA warns that the action is not enough yet.
Altering to port, or changing speed only, in a head-on situation is a violation; each vessel must alter to starboard.
Giving way in a crossing by turning to port (may cross ahead) is a warning; starboard or slowing is expected.
Stand-on stage 0: keeping course and speed is correct; altering early is a violation.
Stand-on stage 1: the give-way vessel is not acting, you may now act.
Stand-on stage 2: collision can no longer be avoided by the give-way vessel alone, you must act; no action by TCPA <= half the alarm is a violation.
In a crossing, turning to port for a vessel on your port side is a violation.
Restricted visibility: altering to port for a vessel forward of the beam (not being overtaken) is a violation.
Restricted visibility: altering towards a vessel abeam or abaft the beam is a violation.
Own speed above the safe speed for the visibility raises a warning.
A collision always counts as a failure whoever was give-way.
Own ship grounding is reported as not navigating safely.
With the autopilot on, the simulator applies the avoiding action for you (informational).
